messages:
maya: Heads-up: node-123 (p4d-2) had two repeated Xid 31 + ECC messages this morning, causing pod evictions. Attaching dmesg/journal snippets below. Can someone grab the short logs and recommend the best quick triage?

maya: dmesg excerpt:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (31) 00000000
[ 1234.567892] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed: 0x32
[ 1234.567894] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.567900] mcelog: CPU 1: Machine check events logged
```

maya: journalctl snippet for nvidia:
```
Mar 18 07:12:11 node-123 kernel: NVRM: Xid (61) 00000000: 0x8f3ef23a
Mar 18 07:12:11 node-123 systemd[1]: Stopped gpu-health-exporter.service
Mar 18 07:12:12 node-123 kubelet[1234]: Evicting pod: OOM+gpu error
```

samir: Thanks. First pass: collect `nvidia-smi -q` output + `dmesg --ctime --kernel` and full journal for the last 15m. Also capture the nvml plugin logs. Use `journalctl -u docker -S "-15m" --no-pager` if containerd/dockerd.

dave: quick commands I ran on node-123 (ssh):
```bash
ssh ops@node-123 \\
  "sudo nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE,ERRORS > /tmp/nv_q.txt; \\
   sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg_tail.txt; \\
   sudo journalctl -k -S "-20m" --no-pager > /tmp/journal_kernel.txt"
```

jin: If you can, also run the GPU health probe we added: `sudo /opt/redwood/bin/gpu_diag --quick --json > /tmp/gpu_diag.json` — it dumps ECC counts and memory checks.

maya: ran that, attaching small snippets inline:
`/tmp/gpu_diag.json` shows `ecc_corrected_count: 124` on GPU 0 and `pending_xid: true`.

samir: Ok that pattern (rising corrected ECC + Xid falloff) usually indicates flaky card or power/PCIe issue, not a CUDA app bug. Two quick options: 1) drain + isolate the node and run extended diagnostics (memtest for GPU) or 2) soft-reset the GPU if the runtime allows and continue monitoring. For production, prefer drain/replace if rate > 1/day.

dave: To drain: `kubectl drain node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (we've got drain playbook). After drain, run tech-proc `nvsmi -r`? note: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0` only works on supported Tesla cards and when no processes are using it.

maya: I tried `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0` but it reported `GPU reset failed: Not Supported`. So soft-reset won't work here.

jin: We should enrich our log ingestion: capture full `dmesg` lines and the `nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS` block into a single telemetry envelope, and tag by `pci_id` and `bios` values. Regex we use in the parser: `(?i)NVRM:\s*Xid \((\d+)\)\s*(0x[0-9a-f]+)?` to pull Xid code and hex payload. Also extract `GPU .*: RmInitAdapter failed: (0x[0-9a-f]+)` as failure token.

samir: Agree. Add an extractor for `ECC.*corrected_count` lines and plot delta over last 24h — triggers auto-drain at threshold. Suggested thresholds: corrected > 50/hour for 1h window -> mark as suspect; Xid > 3 in 24h -> immediate investigation.

maya: Ops decision: draining now, tests scheduled. I'll upload full /tmp bundle to the logship service: `logshipctl send /tmp/{nv_q,dmesg_tail,journal_kernel,gpu_diag}.tar.gz --tag node-123 --type gpu-failure`

logship-bot: Received bundle node-123 at 2026-03-18T07:20:03Z. Creating index entry id=ls-7f9a. Parsing with gpu-extract v2.1.

samir: After we have the bundle, can we run correlation against historical failures in region-us-west-2? If multiple nodes same rack show PCIe resets, escalate to infra-networking (possible switch/PSU).

maya: Noted. I'll flag infra-networking and schedule hardware swap if bench tests fail. Thanks all :thumbsup:

dave: small follow-up: we'll add the sample parsers to the repo `eng-infra/gpu-log-parsers` and include a short unit test with synthetic dmesg lines. Will ping when PR is up.

maya: Great — updating incident card with steps + link to log bundle ls-7f9a.
